answerNotes.EGG: A hen's egg has a shell, white, and yolk. Recipes sometimes use only one inner part rather than the whole egg.
answerNotes.CUP: Cup can name a drinking vessel or a measuring amount. A recipe's measured cup is not simply any small mug.
answerNotes.COLOR: Color names such as red, blue, and yellow describe appearance. They can help with a flower scene without requiring botanical vocabulary.
answerNotes.SPOON: A spoon has a small bowl at one end. It can hold liquid, unlike the prongs of a fork.
answerNotes.WATER: Water is the same liquid whether it is in a drinking glass, a garden hose, or a cooking pot. The container changes the scene, not the substance.
answerNotes.SHELL: Shell means a hard outer covering. The same everyday word can describe the outside of an egg, nut, or crab.
answerNotes.YELLOW: Yellow is a color name rather than a material. The movie's yellow brick road combines a color with a building block.
answerNotes.DRY: Dry can be an adjective or an action. It can describe laundry after airing or what happens when moisture leaves a flower bundle.
answerNotes.EASTER: Colored eggs and chocolate rabbits are seasonal customs. The separately labeled Bible puzzles concern the Christian stories associated with the holiday.

answerNotes.PAPER: Paper can be folded, cut, and written on. Card stock is heavier and stiffer, making it useful for tags and greeting cards.
answerNotes.EAR: Ears receive sound. In an animal clue, the word usually asks for a body part rather than a call or other sound.
answerNotes.TAIL: Tail can name the rear part of an animal or a trailing end of ribbon or a kite. The word describes different things with a similar extending position.
answerNotes.COTTON: Cotton is a plant fiber used in many washable household items. Wool instead comes from an animal's fleece.
answerNotes.GLUE: Glue bonds surfaces together as it sets. Tape holds them with an adhesive already attached to a strip.
answerNotes.SCISSORS: Scissors use two blades moving past one another. Finger loops help control the opening and closing action.
answerNotes.CUT: Cut is an action, unlike a tool name such as scissors or knife. Matching the clue's part of speech helps narrow the answer.
answerNotes.FOLD: Folding brings one part of a sheet over another. A crease is the line left by pressing that fold.
answerNotes.WHITE: White is a color description, not a flower or bird name. Crossings can help when a clue asks for a color rather than a species.
answerNotes.EASTER: Colored eggs and chocolate rabbits are seasonal customs. The separately labeled Bible puzzles concern the Christian stories associated with the holiday.
answerNotes.TABLE: A table provides a raised flat surface. Chairs are the separate furniture used to sit beside it.
answerNotes.PAW: Paw names the foot of an animal such as a cat, fox, or rabbit. A cow or horse instead has a hoof.

answerNotes.EGG: A hen's egg has a shell, white, and yolk. Recipes sometimes use only one inner part rather than the whole egg.
answerNotes.WOOD: Wood comes from trees and has a grain. Following that grain when sanding usually leaves a smoother surface.
answerNotes.PAINT: Paint leaves a colored coating on a surface. A stain usually allows more of wood's natural grain to remain visible.
answerNotes.BRUSH: A brush holds many bristles in one handle. Their width and stiffness affect the marks or cleaning action it makes.
answerNotes.DOT: Dot is the everyday word for a small round mark. On dominoes, the groups of dots indicate each end's value.
answerNotes.COLOR: Color names such as red, blue, and yellow describe appearance. They can help with a flower scene without requiring botanical vocabulary.
answerNotes.PATTERN: A pattern is an arrangement that repeats. In sewing, the same word can also mean a template for cutting fabric pieces.
answerNotes.DRY: Dry can be an adjective or an action. It can describe laundry after airing or what happens when moisture leaves a flower bundle.
answerNotes.EASTER: Colored eggs and chocolate rabbits are seasonal customs. The separately labeled Bible puzzles concern the Christian stories associated with the holiday.
answerNotes.SHELF: A shelf is a horizontal storage surface. A drawer is a compartment that slides in and out.
